name: OurResearch (legal name Impactstory; now operating as OpenAlex)
subcategory: nonprofit open scholarly metadata (OpenAlex), open-access discovery (Unpaywall) and library analytics (Unsub)
origin_detail: Formed in 2011 as ImpactStory by Jason Priem and Heather Piwowar, whose first product was an open-source altmetrics tool. Its IRS 501(c)(3) ruling came in Feb 2014 under the legal name Impactstory (EIN 46-1599252, Sanford, NC; Wikipedia also gives Vancouver as a location). Early funders were the Alfred P. Sloan Foundation and NSF. Products followed: Unpaywall (browser extension and oaDOI service, integrated into Web of Science June 2017), Unsub (2019) and OpenAlex (January 2022, successor to Microsoft Academic Graph). By November 2026 ourresearch.org 301-redirects to openalex.org, and the GitHub organisation 'ourresearch' (created 2012) is named 'OpenAlex'.
flagship_projects: OpenAlex (Jan 2022; CC0 index of ~500M works with authors, institutions, sources and topics)
Unpaywall (open-access location finder; 49M free articles claimed in 2024)
openness_notes: A nonprofit whose data is CC0 ('Our data is CC0'), whose code is open source (e.g. openalex-guts, MIT) and whose governance it calls 'transparent', with an OpenAlex Community Advisory Board. Revenue comes from paid services around the free data: the Unpaywall Data Feed, Unsub and OpenAlex paid API tiers. By 2026 OpenAlex API access is usage-priced: '$1 a day free', prepaid usage, annual subscriptions and Member+/Partner tiers. That limits heavy free API use but not the CC0 data or the downloadable database. Scored 4 (fully open data infrastructure) with that caveat.

license_history.note: Wikipedia: 'the first open-source, web-based tool released by the organization'

risk_events: FY2020-FY2021: no grant income. Revenue of $0.74M-$1.15M came entirely from program services (Unsub/Unpaywall), and net assets fell to $182k (FY2021).
Dec 2021: Microsoft Academic Graph retired. OurResearch launched OpenAlex as its open replacement in January 2022.
FY2024: net assets negative (-$126,729) despite $3.55M revenue. They recovered to $1.17M in FY2025.
Mar 2024: $7.5M Arcadia Fund grant to establish OpenAlex as an open alternative to commercial products. The French Ministry of Higher Education and Research pledged support in 2024.
Top-paid officer per Form 990 summaries changed from co-founder Jason Priem (CEO, FY2022) to a CTO (FY2023-24) and a COO, Kyle Demes (FY2025). The founders' current roles were not confirmed.
2025-26: usage-based API pricing for OpenAlex ('$1 a day free', prepaid usage, annual plans)
Data quality: fabricated ('sneaked') reference metadata in Crossref, which OpenAlex draws on, was reported in 2024
robustness: CC0 data and a downloadable whole-database snapshot mean OpenAlex's content survives the organisation, since anyone can re-host it (e.g. SemOpenAlex's 26 billion RDF triples). The organisation itself is small and was fragile: net assets were negative in FY2024 and grants were 56% of FY2025 revenue. Funding is now more diversified (Arcadia, Schmidt Sciences, Wellcome-funded work, the French ministry, California Digital Library, plus paid tiers) and it is hiring (Nov 2026).
physical_science_relevance: OpenAlex is the open replacement for Microsoft Academic Graph and an alternative to Scopus and Web of Science for bibliometrics. This study's own scripts (scripts/openalex_trends.py) use the OpenAlex API to measure open-access shares of US Physical Sciences, Materials Science and Chemistry output by institution type. For materials and self-driving-lab research it supplies CC0 metadata for literature mining and for assembling paper corpora. Unpaywall's open-access locations let a lab find legal full texts. In 2026 OpenAlex added software as a work type (Schmidt Sciences grant), which helps credit lab code.
openness_effect_assessment: CC0 data and open code let OpenAlex replace MAG at launch and win institutional adopters that a proprietary index at its price could not: Sorbonne dropped Scopus for it (Dec 2023), the Leiden Ranking adopted it (2024) and the French ministry backs it. Openness did not pay for itself, though. The nonprofit ran deficits, had negative net assets in FY2024 and relied on grants for 56% of FY2025 revenue. It now charges for API convenience while keeping the data CC0, an 'open data, paid service' model.
key_takeaway: OurResearch shows a small nonprofit building core open-science infrastructure on a few million dollars a year (FY2025 revenue $4.3M, 56% of it grants) by selling services around CC0 data. Its finances were fragile, with negative net assets in FY2024, until large grants such as Arcadia's $7.5M arrived, and it now prices heavy API use. For a lab, OpenAlex is the open literature database that this very project uses, and its CC0 snapshot protects users from any later pricing change.

funding_sources: Alfred P. Sloan Foundation; National Science Foundation ($300k grant announced 2013, per a cited blog title)
Schmidt Sciences (two-year grant for research software in OpenAlex, 2026)
French Ministry of Higher Education and Research (2024 partnership)
Wellcome-funded funder-metadata project; California Digital Library (corresponding-author work)
Program service revenue: Unpaywall Data Feed, Unsub, OpenAlex paid tiers ($1.89M in FY2025)
notes: No web searches were run for this entry (shared WebSearch budget exhausted); see fetched_urls.

funding_total_usd is the sum of 'contributions/grants' on Impactstory's Form 990s for FY2013-FY2025 (fiscal years ending June) as summarised by ProPublica. It is a cumulative grant total, not equity funding, and multi-year grants may be booked in one year.

No formal announcement of a renaming from OurResearch to OpenAlex was found. The evidence is the ourresearch.org to openalex.org redirect, the GitHub organisation name, and blog.ourresearch.org now serving blog.openalex.org posts.
unpaywall.org pages returned only a title, as a JavaScript app, so Unpaywall's current pricing and status were not confirmed. help.openalex.org lists Unpaywall among the ways to get OpenAlex data.
Employee count was not found; the blog says new software positions will open 'in the next few weeks' (Nov 2026).
